templates_considered: external_calls_handle_errors (LOG-010): fits. Its check (statement.containment, try_catch) covers the error-handling half of the ask. Its statement list is api.request only; I added stream.from_request and webflow.request as the limits text advises.
requests_have_timeout (SEC-013): fits. Its statement.param_bound rule covers the 30-second cap. Its statement list is api.request, stream.from_request, webflow.request, which I kept.
no_destructive_sql, middleware_surfaces_errors, get_endpoints_only_read, inputs_validated, triggers_write_elsewhere: no fit, not related to outbound calls.

AUTH-*, DATA-*, CONF-*, SEC-012 (literal.credential_shape), VND-001 (outbound.vendor_allowlist): no fit for this ask. Noted SEC-012 in the reply because acme_notify_sms has a literal credential in an outbound URL. VND-001 would be relevant to the vendor side but the ask is about timeout and error handling only.

rules.covers: Every external call sits inside a try block so a vendor failure reaches error handling (the 'some kind of error handling' part, presence only)
Every external call has a timeout no longer than 30 seconds (the 'timeout set' part, upper bound)
Every external call sets timeout explicitly. Added because the param_bound rule judges an omitted timeout at its 10-second default and would pass it

ask_parts_not_covered.part: error handling: that the catch branch actually handles the failure (returns a fallback or a clear error)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how: the check confirms only the try_catch placement; what the catch does is not readable as a check

ask_parts_not_covered.part: external calls made through AI agents, MCP servers and direct DB connections, plus api.microservice, api.lambda and cloud.* requests
ask_parts_not_covered.why: other: I scoped to the three statements the templates and the ask point at; those others have a different timeout or none (ai.external.mcp.* and db.external.* take no timeout)

ask_parts_not_covered.part: a vendor being down does not hang the app (the whole-app effect)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: needs runtime/org process: a timeout limits each call, but whether a hung vendor can still exhaust workers or threads is a runtime fact no check reads

assumptions: The customer's 'external API call' means the api.request, stream.from_request and webflow.request statements, the ones the templates name.
A timeout of 30 seconds is an acceptable cap, from the SEC-013 template's summary, not from the customer.
Advisory enforcement is the right starting point, per the skill's rule for new policies.
The pulled workspace reflects the stored definitions (the pull was read-only and I did not evaluate).

function: acme_notify_sms (api.request, no timeout, no try_catch)

api endpoint: payments/fraud_check POST (api.request, timeout = 15, no try_catch)

confusions: The LOG-010 template summary says 'so a vendor failure reaches error handling', which reads as if the check verifies handling. Its limits text says it confirms only the try placement. I wrote the statement to match the limits, not the summary.

The SEC-013 template's rule uses only max: 30 and does not mention that an omitted timeout passes. The limits text says so, but it is easy to miss. I added a param_required rule to close that gap; the template does not suggest it and I was not sure whether to put it in the same policy or a separate one.

The skill says one policy per template and extra rules in a policy of your own key. I put the extra param_required rule inside SEC-013 (the template's key) rather than making a new key. The skill's 'add only what the request asks' seemed to allow it, but this is a judgment call.
xano policy parse (text mode) does not print the severity line, though -o json shows severity medium. I checked with JSON to confirm the value was kept.

Statement names for stream.from_request and webflow.request come from the skill's statement list and the catalogue; I did not verify webflow.request exists in this workspace (no rule warning was raised).
wished_for: A template or recipe for 'every external call has a timeout and error handling' that already includes param_required on timeout, since the bare param_bound rule passes omitted timeouts.
A note in the LOG-010 template or the check that the catch body is not checked, next to the summary's 'reaches error handling' wording.
A catalogue list (or a recipe) of which statements take a timeout and which do not, in one place, so the statement list is not assembled from several sections of the skill.
why_confidence: The two rule families do check what the ask names: a timeout on every external call (with a cap and an explicit-set rule) and a try block around every call. But the error-handling rule checks only that a try block exists, not that the catch handles the failure, and a hang across the app has runtime causes no check reads. Predictions about findings are from reading the pulled code; I did not run xano policy evaluate, which the brief forbids.
